newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil won't sign info tech pact yet - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil won't sign info tech pact yet - report.

text.p: Brazil has no intention for now of signing a pact reducing tariffs on information technology trade to zero by the year 2000, the Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper reported Tuesday.

Citing "sources in the presidential palace", the newspaper said the decision not to join the first round of signings of the Information Technology Agreement (ITA), due to take place in March, was made by the Brazilian government last month.
Estado said "the government does not object in principle and realizes that eventually it will have to join but wants to know first what to expect in exchange."
No official comment was immediately forthcoming but a Foreign Ministry source noted that as Brazil was a net importer of information technology, it stood to benefit little by joining the ITA.
Jose Alfredo Graca Lima, head of the Foreign Ministry's economics department and in charge of negotiations on international trade accords, was unavailable for comment.
The ITA was agreed at December's World Trade Organization (WTO) ministerial summit in Singapore.
Twenty-eight nations signed up, including the United States, the European Union, Japan and Canada and representing the bulk of world trade in information technology.
Tariffs on 173 categories of information technology ranging from computers to telephone headsets are supposed to be eradicated in four stages by the year 2000.
Estado said the Brazilian government was taken by surprise in Singapore when a pact emerged.
Its source said Brasilia was not warned that the United States and others would turn the accord into one of their principal objectives for the Singapore meeting.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce has been ordered to prepare a detailed report on the impact of the ITA on Brazil's fledgling computer software and hardware industry.
The paper added that Washington was trying to convert Brazil's Mercosur partner Argentina to its side in order to pressure Brasilia into falling into line.
Argentina, the second-largest partner in the four-nation Mercosur trade pact, which also includes Uruguay and Paraguay, does not have an information technology industry.
